outcome: Duration of first stage of labor
Duration of second stage of labor
Need for obstetric interventions (instrumental delivery, LSCS)
cohort: The study included 200 pregnant women aged 18 or above with uncomplicated term pregnancies (37 weeks and above) in cephalic presentation, who were in the first stage of labor with fetuses in occipitoanterior and occipitotransverse positions.
finding: Measuring the occiput spine angle during the first stage of labor using transabdominal ultrasound is an effective predictor of the course and outcome of labor, with a larger angle (>126-127 degrees) associated with shorter labor duration and normal vaginal delivery, and a smaller angle (<120 degrees) associated with longer labor and increased obstetric interventions.
mod_finding: A larger occiput spine angle (>126 degrees) was associated with a higher incidence of normal vaginal delivery, whereas a smaller angle (<120 degrees) was associated with a higher incidence of obstetric interventions, including instrumental deliveries and LSCS.
cross-section timing: During the first stage of labor
